topicCandidates: Tax residence under income-tax law, including resident, non-permanent resident, and non-resident classifications and their separation from nationality and immigration status.
The calendar-year national income-tax cycle and the later individual resident-tax cycle administered by the municipality associated with January 1 residence.
Salary withholding, year-end adjustment, employee declarations and deduction evidence, overseas dependants, prior-employer records, and the salary withholding slip.
Final-return filing for employees, including multiple payers, income outside salary, the limited 200,000-yen filing exception, refund returns, and the distinction from municipal declarations.
Records to preserve from arrival, job changes, year end, filing, and departure.
userSituations: A newcomer assumes a residence card or a named visa decides whether they are tax resident.
An employee receives little or no resident-tax bill in the first year and is surprised by a later bill based on prior-year income.
A worker changes employers mid-year and the new employer needs the prior salary withholding slip before completing year-end adjustment.
An employee supports relatives overseas and needs relationship, remittance, translation, or other route-specific evidence for a deduction.
A salary earner has a second employer, freelance income, investment income, foreign income, or an unclaimed deduction and assumes year-end adjustment resolved everything.
A person hears that income of 200,000 yen or less never needs to be reported and misses the narrow scope of that national filing exception or a separate resident-tax declaration.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Income-tax residence turns on domicile and residence facts. Temporary absence can preserve residence, while immigration labels and nationality do not decide the classification.
A non-permanent resident is still a tax resident; the label has a specific nationality and five-of-ten-year test and changes the taxable scope of certain foreign-source income.
Withholding is a collection mechanism, not a final determination of taxable scope or liability.
Year-end adjustment applies only to covered salary and people meeting its conditions. It does not reconcile every income source, deduction, employer, residence period, or international issue.
The 200,000-yen rule is not a tax-free allowance. It is part of limited national final-return exceptions for defined salary earners, and municipal resident-tax reporting can still differ.
Filing a return for another reason generally requires all reportable income to be included rather than omitting income below a popular threshold.
A refund return can be available even when filing is not mandatory, subject to its own time limit and evidence.
Individual resident-tax rates, declarations, collection, relief, notices, and departure handling contain municipal or prefectural implementation details.
jurisdictionVariables: Domicile, length and continuity of residence, nationality, prior ten-year presence, temporary-absence facts, income source, payment location, and remittances.
Calendar year, employer and payer count, salary amount, other income categories, withholding, deductions, prior employment, and departure timing.
Municipality of residence on January 1, prior-year income, salary special collection or ordinary collection, job changes, and local declaration requirements.
Relationship, age, disability or study facts, remittance evidence, and translation for dependants living outside Japan.
Treaty, foreign tax, foreign assets, self-employment, consumption tax, and business facts reserved for the next implementation pass or professional advice.

primarySourceCandidates.organization: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Taxation

contentImpacts.reason: Separate the foundational residence and taxable-scope decision from payment and filing procedures.
Turn the draft overview into a clear national-versus-local calendar and first-year planning guide.
Explain the employee documents and payroll reconciliation workflow without treating it as universal filing completion.
Document employee filing triggers, the limited threshold exception, refunds, records, and filing workflow.
Expose the focused tax sequence in Explore.
Order tax classification, payroll, and filing without presenting every step as universal.
Route common questions to the new canonical guides.
Teach tax-resident terminology without confusing it with immigration residence.
Make the core employee tax record searchable and understandable.

scopeBoundaries: 9B-1 provides general individual employee guidance, not individualized tax calculations, treaty conclusions, or filing preparation.
Foreign-income remittance calculations, foreign tax credits, treaty claims, self-employment, consumption tax, invoice registration, and detailed departure handling remain in 9B-2.
Resident-tax guidance explains the common national framework and requires confirmation with the responsible municipality; it does not claim nationwide uniform forms or relief.
Tax compliance does not establish immigration permission, employment-contract permission, professional licensing, or social-insurance compliance.
Annual thresholds and forms must be tied to current NTA material and must not be presented as timeless.

scopeApproval.note: The editor approved beginning 9B-1 after reviewing and accepting the proposed employee-and-resident fundamentals split.
